messages:
maya: Heads-up — observed repeated tail-latency spikes (5-12x) on some small GPU hosts in apac-edge. Correlates with heavy NVMe write bursts from tenant containers doing checkpointing. :frowning:
raj: ugh. any kernel logs or iostat? sounds like IO stacking with PCIe and GPU traffic.
maya: posting quick snippets — not super long, but pattern is obvious.

```
iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 120.00 5.00 420.00  4.00  81920.00  193.48  8.20  18.3  1.2  39.1  1.5  96.2
```

```
[ 1234.567890] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789 op 1
[ 1234.568000] writeback: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, start 98765432
```

maya: same nodes also show brief GPU stalls in our runtime telemetry (kv cache miss spikes). Not full OOMs, just big latency windows.
raj: probable root cause: shared NVMe/CPU scheduling contention causing long tail for small tenants. Could be exacerbated by host-side DMA bursts from model checkpoint flushes.
lin: two quick mitigations we can try:
- cgroup blkio throttle (write_iops or bps) per tenant pod
- node-level taint + move noisy tenants to nodes with local ephemeral SSDs isolated from GPU fabric
ops-bot: ALERT: host nvme throttling pattern detected on node gpu-apac-13 — auto-annotations applied. :robot_face:
eva: agree with lin. cgroup knobs are low risk but we need to measure perf impact for large-batch users. also concerned about forcing writes to network storage (S3) — that'll hit egress and increase cost.
maya: proposed immediate steps:
1) identify top 10 tenants by wkB/s on affected nodes (already ran `duf`/iostat)
2) cordon affected nodes and trigger scale-up to dedicated-pool for those tenants
3) apply conservative blkio limits for all tenants on affected host: `echo "8:0 5000" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/blkio.throttle.write_iops_device` as a rolling pilot
4) run stress-fio job on repro node to validate GPU latency impact
raj: +1. For (3) prefer orchestration via kube `Pod` resource annotations that our runtime reads and enforces via a sidecar — avoids manual sysfs echoes.
lin: we should also add a telemetry flag to tag NVMe-heavy requests so Optimize can suggest checkpoint cadence changes per model. low-cost ops.
maya: I'll open a runbook PR with steps and a small script to detect write storms and create a quick temp `dedicated` placement label. will also include rollback: remove blkio file, uncordon nodes.
eva: timeline? can we have a canary on 2 nodes in 1 hour?
maya: yes — will do canary tonight 23:00 UTC. will ping when cordon + blkio set. :eyes:
ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled canary - 3733333333-canary-gpu-nvme-throttle at 2024-09-12T23:00:00Z (automated)
maya: thanks — will add observed metrics after canary. any objections?
raj: none from me. track cost delta for S3 fallback in the canary notes.
lin: no objections. add alert threshold for `nvme_write_bytes/s > 50MB` on nodes to auto-run detection script.
maya: will do. closing for now, will update thread after canary. :thumbsup:
